audit_findings.title: Series B treatment may mismatch the common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 14.711219 million preferred units; $315.0 million liquidation preference; $29.466 million 2025 preferred distributions; preferred units are 6.4% of the 229.268275 million denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Affects both the OE numerator and per-unit denominator, or alternatively requires deduction of the preferred claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Partnership cannot pay any distributions on any junior securities, including common units, prior to paying the quarterly distribution payable to the preferred units, including any previously accrued and unpaid distributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The senior claim is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the $299.5 million OE anchor is before or after preferred distributions. The $29.466 million annual distribution equals 9.8% of anchor OE, while the $315.0 million liquidation preference equals 6.7% to 10.4% of scenario equity value. Deducting preferred economics after already subtracting distributions would understate value; including preferred units while valuing only common cash flow would also understate value; omitting the senior claim from common-only value would overstate value. The scale is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete OE-to-equity reconciliation for every historical year and rerun all scenarios under one consistent method: pre-preferred OE with an as-converted denominator, or post-preferred OE with only common-equivalent awards in the denominator and the applicable preferred claim in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may omit the cost of replacing depleting assets
audit_findings.magnitude: $126.225 million of 2025 acquisition and development costs, equal to 42.1% of $299.5 million anchor OE, versus computed base-growth reinvestment of approximately $29.46 million using 3% growth divided by 30.5% RONTA
audit_findings.mechanism: Understates the reinvestment deduction in forecast OE and terminal value while supporting positive production or cash-flow growth.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Partnership acquired mineral and royalty interests that consisted of primarily unproved oil and natural gas properties in East Texas from various sellers for an aggregate of $ 114.5 million, including capitalized direct transaction costs, and were considered asset acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates depletion pressure: 2025 production declined 10.4% and proved reserves declined from 57.380 to 54.845 MMBoe despite additions. It also reports $114.468 million of property acquisition costs and $11.757 million of development costs in 2025. Those expenditures are not automatically maintenance spending, but their scale materially exceeds the modeled base-growth reinvestment charge. Because nearly half of base value and more than half of bull value comes from terminal assumptions, an understated replacement requirement is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify 2023-2026 mineral acquisitions, leasehold purchases, seismic spending, development costs, farmout consideration, and acquisition-related unit issuance between maintenance and growth; calculate an all-in realized RONTA after that spending; then rerun growth and terminal value with the reconciled replacement requirement.

audit_findings.title: Elevated lease-bonus income may be embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.351 million of 2025 lease-bonus and other income, including an $8.890 million increase over 2024; complete removal would reduce computed base value by approximately $1.31 per unit, from $18.36 to about $17.05
audit_findings.mechanism: Raises anchor OE if episodic lease-bonus or surface-use proceeds are retained and then grown as recurring operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Lease bonus revenue can vary substantively between periods because it is derived from individual transactions with operators, some of which may be significant.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the anchor remains unverified, but the filed amount provides a conservative upper bound. Even removing the entire $21.351 million rather than merely the $8.890 million year-over-year increase would leave computed base value around $17.05, above the $14.65 price, while lowering the 30%-MOS buy level to about $11.94, still below the price. On this isolated finding, the stated valuation posture would not change.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $21.351 million by transaction into the 2025 OE worksheet, identify lease bonuses, delay rentals, and surface-use proceeds separately, and document a multi-year normalized amount; rerun only if the retained amount exceeds the filed 2025 total through another classification error.

audit_findings.title: Temporary hedge gains may be projected as permanent earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.602 million unrealized gain and $10.989 million realized gain in 2025; if both were included and capitalized, the computed base-value effect would be approximately $2.92 per unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Inflates anchor OE and all forecast cash flows if unrealized mark-to-market gains or finite realized settlements are treated as perpetual operating earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we recognized $11.0 million of realized gains and $36.6 million of unrealized gains from our commodity derivatives, compared to $45.2 million of realized gains and $50.9 million of unrealized losses in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that management's Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation removed the $36.602 million unrealized gain while retaining the $10.989 million cash settlement, and reported DCF of $300.039 million is close to the $299.5 million anchor. That suggests, but does not prove, that unrealized gains were excluded from OE. No OE construction schedule confirms the treatment or shows how the finite realized hedge benefit transitions to normalized commodity economics. The realized component alone is 3.7% of anchor OE; accidental inclusion of both components would be 15.9%, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Provide the 2025 OE bridge from GAAP net income through derivative adjustments, identify every realized and unrealized amount retained, map outstanding hedge settlements through 2027, and rerun the forecast with an explicit transition to the selected normalized price basis.

audit_findings.title: Revenue accrual estimates could distort the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes latest-year revenue and OE through subsequent operator-statement true-ups, directly affecting the sole $299.5 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As a non-operator, the Partnership has limited visibility into the timing of when new wells start producing and production statements may not be received for 30 to 90 days or more after the date production is delivered.
audit_findings.explanation: The estimation exposure is demonstrated: accrued revenue was $62.679 million at December 31, 2025, equal to 20.9% of anchor OE, and statements may arrive 30 to 90 days or more after production. That balance is not an error amount, however, and the supplied 2026 filing does not isolate collections, reversals, or prior-period true-ups attributable to the 2025 estimate. The direction and size of any anchor error therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the December 31, 2025 accrued-revenue balance by operator and production month to 2026 cash receipts and statements, quantify estimate-to-actual true-ups affecting 2025 production, prices, and deductions, and rerun all scenarios if the corrected 2025 OE is materially different from $299.5 million.
